content.text: {"predictors": [{"name": "R&D Growth Acceleration", "construction": "Using Compustat annual data, compute R&D expense (XRD) scaled by total assets (AT). Calculate the year-over-year change in this ratio, then the change in that change (second difference) over three consecutive fiscal years. Rank stocks cross-sectionally at each June formation date using data lagged at least six months.", "rationale": "Accelerating R&D intensity signals firms ramping investment in growth options that the market underappreciates due to expensing of R&D and slow updating of expectations about intangible payoffs.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of R&D growth acceleration"}, {"name": "Inventory-to-Sales Divergence", "construction": "From Compustat, compute the growth rate of inventory (INVT) minus the growth rate of sales (SALE) over the trailing fiscal year. Standardize cross-sectionally. Form portfolios at June using data lagged six months.", "rationale": "When inventories grow faster than sales, it signals demand overestimation and future markdowns/writeoffs, so such firms underperform, while firms drawing down inventory relative to sales face improving operations.", "higher_returns_for": "low values (inventory growing slower than sales)"}, {"name": "Order-Backlog Intensity", "construction": "From Compustat, take order backlog (OB) divided by total assets (AT), measured at fiscal year-end. Rank stocks cross-sectionally among firms reporting backlog. Form portfolios in June with a six-month reporting lag.", "rationale": "A large order backlog relative to assets represents contracted-but-unrecognized future revenue that is not yet reflected in earnings-based valuation, leading to positive future returns as the backlog converts to sales.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of backlog intensity"}, {"name": "Dividend Initiation Consistency Streak", "construction": "Using CRSP dividend distribution codes, count the number of consecutive years a firm has paid a dividend without a cut, then interact with the dividend yield relative to its own five-year average. Rank cross-sectionally each month.", "rationale": "A long uninterrupted dividend streak combined with a yield above the firm's own history signals financial discipline and temporary undervaluation, capturing a quality-plus-value effect not yet formalized.", "higher_returns_for": "high streak with elevated relative yield"}, {"name": "Return Seasonality in Fiscal-Report Months", "construction": "For each stock, identify the calendar months in which it historically reported earnings (from Compustat report dates over the prior five years). Compute the average excess return the stock earned in those same-report months historically, cross-sectionally ranked.", "rationale": "Firms with recurring positive returns in their information-release months exhibit persistent under-reaction to predictable seasonal information flow, generating repeatable outperformance.", "higher_returns_for": "high historical report-month return"}, {"name": "Asset Turnover Momentum", "construction": "Compute asset turnover as sales (SALE) divided by average total assets (AT) for the trailing year and the prior year from Compustat. Take the change in asset turnover. Rank cross-sectionally at June with a six-month lag.", "rationale": "Improving asset utilization is a leading indicator of margin expansion and operating efficiency that the market prices with a delay, driving positive future returns.", "higher_returns_for": "high (positive change in asset turnover)"}, {"name": "Idiosyncratic Volatility Trend", "construction": "Estimate monthly idiosyncratic volatility as the standard deviation of market-model residuals from daily CRSP returns each month. Compute the slope of a regression of monthly IVOL on time over the trailing 12 months. Rank cross-sectionally.", "rationale": "Rising idiosyncratic volatility signals increasing information uncertainty and deteriorating fundamentals, so firms with rising IVOL trends subsequently underperform relative to those with declining uncertainty.", "higher_returns_for": "low (declining idiosyncratic volatility trend)"}, {"name": "Share Issuance Acceleration", "construction": "From CRSP, compute the change in split-adjusted shares outstanding over the trailing 12 months, and separately over the 12 months before that. Take the difference (acceleration in net issuance). Rank cross-sectionally each month.", "rationale": "Accelerating share issuance indicates managers exploiting rich equity valuations and dilution not yet impounded, extending the issuance anomaly to its second-order dynamics.", "higher_returns_for": "low (decelerating or negative issuance)"}, {"name": "Cash Productivity", "construction": "Compute sales (SALE) divided by cash and short-term investments (CHE) from Compustat, measured at fiscal year-end. Rank cross-sectionally at June with a six-month lag, within industry.", "rationale": "Firms generating more sales per dollar of cash hold less idle capital and deploy resources efficiently; excess cash hoards signal agency problems and lower future returns.", "higher_returns_for": "high cash productivity"}, {"name": "Analyst Coverage Change Relative to Size", "construction": "Using I/B/E/S, count the number of analysts issuing FY1 estimates in the current month minus the count 12 months prior, then divide by the log of market capitalization from CRSP. Rank cross-sectionally.", "rationale": "Rising analyst attention relative to firm size predicts increasing institutional demand and information incorporation, driving prices upward as coverage-driven visibility expands the investor base.", "higher_returns_for": "high (increasing coverage per unit size)"}]}
